title: Burst reserve loss after scale-controller restart causes reserved-pool replenishment gap
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a routine rolling restart of the scale-controller in us-west-2, several dedicated reserved pools experienced an unexpected drop in burst reserve balance for a subset of tenants. Affected customers began receiving increased tail latency and 503s when bursts were consumed. The incident was reported by an enterprise customer (Acme Retail) at 2026-03-10T09:14Z and escalated to P0 due to SLA exposure.

What happened (short):
- The scale-controller restart sequence triggered leader-election and graceful shutdown hooks.
- In a race condition, in-memory burst ledger shards for some reserved pools were not flushed to the persistent ledger store before the controller process terminated.
- When a new controller leader came up, it reconstructed pool state from persisted ledger shards but the unflushed deltas were missing, leading to transient negative/zero burst reserves for tenants who had recent burst activity.
- The autoscaler reacted to perceived headroom shortfalls by not triggering expected warmups and by redirecting traffic to cold pools, causing customer-facing errors and latency spikes.

Root cause hypothesis (confirmed by log correlation):
1) PreStop hook path allowed the controller to SIGTERM but did not block until ledger flush completed under load (race).
2) Burst ledger flush is best-effort and not transactional with leadership handoff; there is no final atomic checkpoint guaranteeing the latest in-memory deltas are persisted.
3) Under high burst churn, the in-memory delta buffer was non-empty when the process exit raced ahead of the flush future.

Impact:
- Multiple reserved pools in us-west-2 experienced burst-reserve deficit affecting ~6 medium/large tenants for a 3–12 minute window.
- One enterprise customer reported 12% error rate on burst-heavy routes and raised a formal escalation.
- No data loss of user data; only capacity accounting/regeneration shortfall.

Immediate mitigations (executed 2026-03-10):
- Recovered burst balances by replaying short-term request logs and applying missing deltas to persistent ledger for affected pools (manual corrective job run by SRE team).
- Scoped canary rollout of controller with increased preStop wait and synchronous ledger flush to 10% of clusters.
- Customer comms: sent interim update and ETA for full fix; scheduled conference with impacted customers.

Planned permanent fixes and follow-ups:
- Hotfix (priority): Make ledger flush synchronous during PreStop and block process exit until flush completes or a safe timeout is reached. Add idempotent replay marker so partial writes don't cause double-apply on recovery. (Target: 2026-03-13)
- Controller leader handoff redesign: persist a checkpointed sequence number and require new leader to reconcile deltas from buffered logs if checkpoint older than X. (Target: 2026-Q2)
- Add end-to-end regression test that simulates SIGTERM during high-burst churn and asserts ledger consistency after restart. (Target: 2026-03-20)
- Observability: emit 'unflushed_delta_count' and 'last_flush_duration' metrics with alerting if > thresholds; create dashboard tile for burst-reconcile latency. (Target: 2026-03-15)
- Runbook updates: add a step to detect corrupted burst ledger state and a safe automated reconcile tool for SRE. (Target: 2026-03-16)

Rollout plan:
1) Land hotfix behind a feature flag; deploy to staging and run workload replay tests.
2) Canary deploy to a non-critical region (eu-west-1) with synthetic burst traffic for 24h.
3) Gradual roll to us-west-2 with 5–10% traffic canaries for first 1h, then 50% for 4h before full roll.

Customer comms and SLA remediation:
- Commit to a timeline and propose a credits package for the impacted customer contingent on final postmortem.
- Offer a technical postmortem and walkthrough with the customer success and SRE leads.

Notes and open questions:
- How often do we perform graceful shutdown acceptance tests in CI that include forced SIGTERM? (Answer: not consistently for scale-controller; add to CI matrix.)
- Should burst ledger be moved to the primary durable store (etcd) rather than our custom ledger service? Trade-offs: latency and throughput vs stronger durability guarantees.
- Consider backfilling a short-term streaming replication to ensure leader has all deltas before taking over.
